commit.message:
fix(browser): P0 tab-neutrality — failed bootstrap pre-effects close their own tabs

Live-incident leg (2026-09-17, v0.7.0-dev.35230443849.1): the one-shot
continuity fence (526042ee) removed the cross-process replay amplifier,
but the live host's 26 auth/login tabs also carry an intra-process leg:
every supervisor bootstrap retry created a fresh dedicated-root tab, the
logout auth redirect made waitForBootstrapRoot fail
(BOOTSTRAP_ROOT_NOT_READY) and the failed-attempt tab was never closed,
leaking one tab per maintenance tick until tab_capacity_exceeded froze
supervisor bootstrap. A second vector: once a conversation is bound,
supervisorTab recreated the bound conversation tab on every tick after
the original redirected to /auth/login.

Repair:

1. Close-by-proof: a bootstrap pre-effect failure closes exactly the tab
   that THIS attempt created (never a preferred/existing root, never a
   selected tab, never a fleet tab). CLOSE_TAB is best-effort with an
   in-memory ledger retried before the next attempt, so a transiently
   wedged command plane cannot turn one leak into unbounded growth.

2. Auth-redirect reuse: when the bound conversation tab is gone but a
   non-fleet auth-redirect tab exists, supervisorTab reuses it as the
   observation target instead of creating a new tab per tick. The session
   monitor classifies it (NOT_CHATGPT_CONVERSATION); every navigation-
   class recovery stays gated on auth surfaces (reload-auth-redirect-gate).

3. Honest recovery boundary: a successful bootstrap bind clears the stale
   supervisor_bootstrap last_error so the state projection cannot keep
   reporting an incident that is already over.

Tests: 5 new contract tests (supervisor-bootstrap-tab-neutrality) —
tab-neutral retries (repeated logged-out attempts leave zero tabs),
bounded ledger retry, user-claimed tab survival, auth-redirect reuse with
zero NEW_TAB, stale error clearing. Full npm-test suite: 2303 tests,
2301 pass, 0 fail, 2 Windows skips.
